issue.title: [Bugfix][V1] Release in-process LLM resources on deletion

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: mrv2
labels.description: Model Runner V2 specific

issue.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #21073.

With `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`, deleting a directly constructed `LLM` did not release its GPU resources. The in-process engine and worker froze their object graph into Python's permanent GC generation, while deletion did not run the full engine teardown. References held by the engine and worker remained reachable, and the process-global CUDA graph pool could outlive the engine that created it. Together, these gaps blocked construction of another `LLM` in the same process.

This change:

- adds idempotent `LLM.shutdown()` and `LLMEngine.shutdown()` paths and calls them from the destructors;
- skips persistent GC heap freezing for the in-process engine and worker;
- runs the existing compiled-model cleanup finalizer before teardown;
- drops torn-down executor, worker, scheduler, and DP-group references before cache cleanup; and
- resets the process-global CUDA graph pool so a later engine cannot reuse a destroyed pool.

Multiprocess engines keep the GC-freeze optimization. The in-process path may spend more time scanning the engine object graph during cyclic GC, in exchange for making deletion reclaim its resources.

This is not duplicated by #54162 or #54246. Those PRs added weak compiled-model finalization and layer-level KV-cache cleanup, respectively, but current `main` with both changes still reproduces the bare-deletion failure. #45195 and #35676 clean up compiled-model hooks on the `VllmRunner` path; they do not route a directly constructed `LLM` through full shutdown.

## Test Plan

<details>
<summary>Click to expand: full reproduction environment, commands, and output</summary>

### Environment

- Hardware: 1× NVIDIA H200, 140.40 GiB
- OS/architecture: Linux x86_64
- Python: 3.12.3
- PyTorch: `2.13.0+cu130`
- CUDA reported by PyTorch: 13.0
- Model: `hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM` (pre-downloaded and loaded from a local path during validation)
- Tensor parallel size: 1
- Engine mode: V1 in-process (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`)
- Baseline revision: `main` at `56058fd572`
- Updated base revision: `main` at `5707355209`
- Candidate revision: `7e8ff48bb6`

Each revision was installed in its own isolated checkout and virtual environment:

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto
uv pip install -r requirements/test/cuda.in
```

Standalone reproducer (`repro.py`):

```python
import gc

import torch
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams


MODEL = "hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM"


def used_gib() -> float:
    free, total = torch.cuda.mem_get_info()
    return (total - free) / 1024**3


llm = LLM(MODEL, gpu_memory_utilization=0.6)
llm.generate(["Hello my name is"], SamplingParams(max_tokens=1))
print(f"after construct: {used_gib():.2f} GiB")

del llm
gc.collect()
torch.accelerator.empty_cache()
print(f"after del: {used_gib():.2f} GiB")

llm = LLM(MODEL, gpu_memory_utilization=0.6)
llm.generate(["Hello again"], SamplingParams(max_tokens=1))
print("second LLM constructed and generated")
llm.shutdown()
```

Run it with:

```bash
VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 .venv/bin/python repro.py
```

Observed baseline result at `56058fd572`:

```text
after del: 84.26 GiB
ValueError: Free memory on device cuda:0 (55.54/139.80 GiB) on startup
is less than desired GPU memory utilization (0.6, 83.88 GiB)
```

Observed candidate result at `7e8ff48bb6`:

```text
direct-delete passed: send_one_request=False
GPU memory after deletion: 1.46 GiB
direct-delete passed: send_one_request=True
GPU memory after deletion: 1.44 GiB
second LLM constructed, generated, and shut down
third LLM constructed after explicit shutdown
```

</details>

```bash
VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 \
  pytest -q tests/v1/shutdown/test_delete.py \
  -k test_llm_delete_inprocess_direct

pytest -q tests/v1/engine/test_llm_engine_finalizer_is_weak.py
ruff format --check \
  tests/conftest.py tests/v1/shutdown/test_delete.py \
  vllm/entrypoints/llm.py vllm/v1/engine/core.py \
  vllm/v1/engine/core_client.py vllm/v1/engine/llm_engine.py \
  vllm/v1/executor/uniproc_executor.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/shutdown.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py
ruff check \
  tests/conftest.py tests/v1/shutdown/test_delete.py \
  vllm/entrypoints/llm.py vllm/v1/engine/core.py \
  vllm/v1/engine/core_client.py vllm/v1/engine/llm_engine.py \
  vllm/v1/executor/uniproc_executor.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/shutdown.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py
git diff --check
```

The GPU regression covers deletion both before and after one request, then constructs another engine. It also constructs a third engine after explicit `shutdown()` to catch reuse of a stale CUDA graph pool.

## Test Result

On the baseline `main` revision `56058fd572` with one NVIDIA H200, PyTorch 2.13.0, and CUDA 13.0, direct deletion left 84.26 GiB in use. A second `LLM` failed its startup check because 55.54 GiB was free while 83.88 GiB was requested.

issue.title: [Fix] generate() prefills the full prompt instead of only the last token

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issue.body:
## Summary

On transformers 5.x, `model.generate()` on any FLA causal LM silently drops the prompt. On the first decoding step it forwards only the last prompt token with an empty recurrent state, so generation is conditioned on a single token rather than on the prompt. Every model that uses `FLAGenerationMixin` (GatedDeltaNet, GLA, RetNet, GSA, HGRN2, Comba, RWKV7, ...) is affected.

Root cause is in `FLAGenerationMixin.prepare_inputs_for_generation`. When `cache_position` is not supplied (which is the case under transformers 5.x for these models), it falls back to the old "keep only the last token if the cache is not empty" behavior, but tests emptiness with `len(past_key_values) > 0`. For `FLACache`, `__len__` returns the number of layer slots, and those slots are allocated before any token is processed, so it is already non-zero at the prefill step. The prefill step is therefore mistaken for a decode step and the prompt is truncated to its last token.

The fix tests emptiness with `past_key_values.get_seq_length() > 0` (seen tokens) instead of `len(...) > 0` (layer count), in both the transformers 4.56+ branch and the legacy branch. At prefill the seen-token count is 0 so the full prompt is kept; during decode it is positive so only the last token is forwarded, which is exactly what the surrounding comment intends ("only last token if the past is not empty").

Minimal repro:

```python
import torch
from fla.models import GatedDeltaNetConfig
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM

torch.manual_seed(0)
config = GatedDeltaNetConfig(hidden_size=256, num_hidden_layers=2, num_heads=4)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(config).eval().to(torch.float32).cuda()

torch.manual_seed(1)
ids = torch.randint(1, config.vocab_size, (1, 16), device="cuda")
with torch.no_grad():
    # correct greedy first token = argmax of a full-prompt forward
    ref = model(input_ids=ids, use_cache=True).logits[:, -1].argmax(-1).item()
    gen = model.generate(ids, attention_mask=torch.ones_like(ids),
                         max_new_tokens=1, do_sample=False)[0, -1].item()
print("full-prompt argmax:", ref, "| generate first token:", gen)
# before this fix: 826 != 3675   (generate ignores the prompt)
# after  this fix: 826 == 826    (generate prefills the prompt)
```

## Test plan

A regression test was added (`run_test_generate_matches_forward` in `tests/models/test_modeling_base.py`, wired in as `test_generate_prefill` for GatedDeltaNet): a greedy `generate()` must match a manual greedy decode that prefills the full prompt. It fails before the fix and passes after.

- `pytest tests/models/test_modeling_gated_deltanet.py::test_generate_prefill -q` passes with the fix, fails without it.
- `pytest tests/models/test_modeling_gated_deltanet.py::test_generation -q` still passes (no regression to the existing cache path).
- end-to-end check across GatedDeltaNet, GLA, RetNet, GSA, HGRN2, Comba and RWKV7: greedy `generate()` now matches a manual greedy decode token for token; a standard transformers model under the same transformers version already behaved correctly, confirming the issue was FLA specific.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on the touched files.

## Breaking changes

None.

issue.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve logprobs when top_logprobs is null

`/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses` both accept `top_logprobs: null`. When a client explicitly requests output logprobs and serializes this optional field as JSON null, current main returns 200 but silently omits generated-token logprobs.

The request conversion uses `top_logprobs` directly as `SamplingParams.logprobs`, so `null` becomes `None` and disables logprob computation. Chat serving also checks `top_logprobs is not None` before rendering logprobs into the response.

This treats `top_logprobs: null` like an omitted `top_logprobs` only when output logprobs are requested: sampled-token logprobs are computed with zero extra top candidates. Requests that do not ask for output logprobs still keep logprobs disabled.

issue.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Keep length finish_reason for max_tokens-truncated streaming tool calls

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issue.body:
## Purpose

When `tool_choice` is `auto`/`required` and `max_tokens` cuts generation off inside the tool-call JSON, streaming `/v1/chat/completions` reports `finish_reason="tool_calls"` as soon as any tool-call delta was streamed, even though the JSON never closed. A streaming client cannot tell the call was truncated and may execute an incomplete or empty tool call (at `max_tokens=10` only the function name was emitted, yet the terminal chunk reports `tool_calls` with `arguments="{}"`).

This is wrong on two counts: OpenAI's function-calling docs specify `finish_reason="length"` for a tool call cut off by `max_tokens`, and vLLM's own non-streaming path already returns `length` for the same request. Only the streaming terminal branch diverges, because it treats "a tool delta was streamed" as "the tool call finished".

The fix gates the synthetic `tool_calls` on the engine having stopped normally (`output.finish_reason == "stop"`), matching the non-streaming path's parity. Completed tool calls finish with `stop` and are unaffected; only truncated or aborted ones now report their real reason. This is independent of #42213 (which only flushes buffered raw text when no tool delta was streamed); the two touch the same branch but cover disjoint cases.

Fixes #9053.

## Test Plan

E2E on a real OpenAI server (`Qwen3-0.6B`, `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes`), sending the same prompt with `stream=false` and `stream=true` across a sweep of `max_tokens`, comparing the terminal `finish_reason` of each.

## Test Result

E2E, same workload before and after the fix, streaming terminal `finish_reason` vs the non-streaming `finish_reason` for the same request:

| max_tokens | non-stream | stream (before) | stream (after) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | length | **tool_calls** | length |
| 12 | length | **tool_calls** | length |
| 16 | length | **tool_calls** | length |
| 24 | length | **tool_calls** | length |
| 32 | tool_calls | tool_calls | tool_calls |
| 48 | tool_calls | tool_calls | tool_calls |

Truncated rows (10/12/16/24) go from `tool_calls` to `length`, matching non-streaming; completed rows (32/48) stay `tool_calls`.

<details>
<summary>End-to-end reproduction (hardware, environment, script, before/after output)</summary>

Hardware: 1x RTX 4090. Model: `Qwen3-0.6B`.

Server:

```bash
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model Qwen3-0.6B --served-model-name qwen \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8025 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --enforce-eager --max-model-len 2048 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.30
```

Client (paired stream/non-stream per `max_tokens`, `temperature=0`, `tool_choice="required"`):

```python

TOOLS = [{
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
        "name": "get_weather",
        "description": "Get weather",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "city": {"type": "string", "enum": ["Vienna"]},
                "unit": {"type": "string", "enum": ["celsius"]},
            },
            "required": ["city", "unit"],
            "additionalProperties": False,
        },
    },
}]

def post(payload):
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        "http://127.0.0.1:8025/v1/chat/completions",
        data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST",
    )
    return urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120)

def read_stream(resp):
    terminal, args = None, []
    for raw in resp:
        line = raw.decode(errors="replace").strip()
        if not line.startswith("data: "):
            continue
        body = line[6:]

    with post({**common, "stream": True}) as r:
```

issue.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Trim token_ids/logprobs left past a stop string under speculative decoding

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issue.body:
## Purpose

With `ngram` speculative decoding, a single decode step can accept several tokens at once. When a stop string completes in the middle of that accepted batch, V1 truncates `output_text` to the stop boundary but leaves the tokens generated after the stop in `RequestOutput.outputs[0].token_ids`. When logprobs are requested, those past-stop token logprobs are returned as well.

The root cause is that incremental detokenization appends the whole accepted token batch before stop-string evaluation. The stop-string helper returns a character truncation point, so text gets trimmed but the token ids and per-step logprobs are not mapped back to the stop boundary.

This records the text start offset for each newly accepted token, drops tokens whose text starts after the matched stop string, and propagates the dropped-token count so the per-step `new_token_ids` and `new_logprobs` are trimmed consistently for streaming, non-streaming, and logprobs outputs. It only applies when EngineCore has not already ended the step on a stop token, preserving the existing stop-token termination behavior.

## Test Plan

I ran a real `LLM(...)` reproduction with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `ngram` speculative decoding, `temperature=0`, `stop=[" ha ha ha"]`, and `logprobs=2`. The upstream main check reproduces the leak because the speculative path returns six generated token ids and six logprobs while the non-spec baseline returns three; this branch passes with both paths returning three.

I also ran the focused detokenizer regression file, the existing min-tokens detokenizer file, and scoped pre-commit hooks for the three changed Python files.

## Test Result

The real-engine reproduction shows the baseline/spec mismatch on main and `PASS fixed behavior` on this branch. In the failing main run, both `include_stop_str_in_output` modes return correct text and `finish_reason="stop"`, but the speculative output leaks `[6386, 6386, 6386]` past the stop boundary.

<details>
<summary>End-to-end reproduction</summary>

Hardware: one NVIDIA RTX 4090. Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` cached locally at `/root/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen3-0.6B`. Settings: `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`, `enforce_eager=True`, `temperature=0`, `stop=[" ha ha ha"]`, `include_stop_str_in_output` tested both ways, `logprobs=2`, `ngram` speculative config `{"method": "ngram", "num_speculative_tokens": 6, "prompt_lookup_min": 1, "prompt_lookup_max": 4}`.

`sd_stop_boundary_probe.py`:

```python
import argparse
import gc
import json
import os

import torch

os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL", "ERROR")
os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS", "1")

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams


PROMPT = "ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha"
STOP = " ha ha ha"


def build_llm(model: str, speculative: bool) -> LLM:
    spec = None
    if speculative:
        spec = {
            "method": "ngram",
            "num_speculative_tokens": 6,
            "prompt_lookup_min": 1,
            "prompt_lookup_max": 4,
        }
    return LLM(
        model=model,
        max_model_len=2048,
        max_num_seqs=4,
        max_num_batched_tokens=256,
        gpu_memory_utilization=0.25,
        enforce_eager=True,
        speculative_config=spec,
    )


def cleanup_llm(llm: LLM) -> None:
    del llm
    gc.collect()
    torch.accelerator.empty_cache()


def run_case(llm: LLM, include_stop: bool, logprobs: int | None) -> dict:
    params = SamplingParams(
        temperature=0,
        max_tokens=16,
        stop=[STOP],
        include_stop_str_in_output=include_stop,
        skip_special_tokens=False,
        logprobs=logprobs,
    )
    output = llm.generate([PROMPT], params, use_tqdm=False)[0].outputs[0]
    result = {
        "text": output.text,
        "token_ids": list(output.token_ids),
        "finish_reason": output.finish_reason,
        "stop_reason": output.stop_reason,
    }
    if logprobs is not None:
        result["logprobs_len"] = len(output.logprobs or [])
    return result


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--expect", choices=["match", "leak"], required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--logprobs", type=int, default=None)
    args = parser.parse_args()

            == len(spec_rows[mode]["token_ids"])
            for mode in ("exclude", "include")
        )

    if args.expect == "match" and matches and logprobs_match:
        print("PASS fixed behavior")
        return 0
    if args.expect == "leak" and not matches:

    print(
```

issue.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Derive num_speculative_tokens from a speculators draft config

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issue.body:
## Purpose

Refs #40382. The primary issue there, no Ampere attention backend for a non-causal `head_dim=256` draft, is already resolved on current main by #40394. This PR fixes the remaining `num_speculative_tokens` auto-detect gap.

Serving a speculators-format draft (Eagle3, DFlash, PEAGLE, ...) through `--speculative-config` with the target as the top-level `--model` fails to start unless the user also restates `num_speculative_tokens`, even though the draft config already declares it under `speculators_config.proposal_methods[0].speculative_tokens`.

The existing auto-detect path only runs when the speculator repo itself is the top-level `--model` and `maybe_override_with_speculators` handles it. With the target as `--model` and the draft supplied via `--speculative-config`, `SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__` loads the draft as a `SpeculatorsConfig` built from `transformer_layer_config`, so the proposal-method `speculative_tokens` count is dropped before `num_speculative_tokens` can default from it.

This carries the speculators proposal count into the draft config and defaults `num_speculative_tokens` from that count when the user did not provide an explicit value. A user-provided value still takes precedence, and the behavior is generic across speculators algorithms.

## Test Plan

Validated `EngineArgs.create_engine_config()`, the shared config-build path used by `vllm serve` and offline `LLM(...)` before engine startup. The repro uses target model `unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`, speculators draft `nm-testing/Llama3_2_1B_speculator.eagle3`, and omits `num_speculative_tokens`.

## Test Result

On base/main (`091386a99b9542691bb1e935ca44d0efbba6e111`), the command fails in `SpeculativeConfig` with `num_speculative_tokens` missing. With this PR's two-file diff applied to the same checkout, it creates `SpeculativeConfig(..., num_spec_tokens=3)` and sets the draft `num_lookahead_tokens` to `3`.

issue.title: [Bugfix][Qwen2.5-VL] Honor video fps for temporal M-RoPE

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: documentation
labels.description: Improvements or additions to documentation

labels.name: ready
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

labels.name: multi-modality
labels.description: Related to multi-modality (#4194)

labels.name: qwen
labels.description: Related to Qwen models

issue.body:
## Purpose

Qwen2.5-VL currently loses video metadata before calling the HuggingFace processor. Since the HF video processor refactor, `second_per_grid_ts` is computed from `video_metadata.sampled_fps`; when vLLM drops that metadata, pre-decoded videos fall back to a default sampled fps instead of the request/video fps. That value drives the temporal M-RoPE scale used by the model, so videos tagged at 1fps and 30fps get the same temporal spacing in vLLM.

This fixes the Qwen2.5-VL path by keeping video metadata in the data parser, splitting `(video, metadata)` tuples before the HF processor call, and forwarding `video_metadata` so HF can compute `sampled_fps` from the real frame metadata. The dummy video builder also attaches synthetic metadata, matching the Qwen3-VL pattern and keeping memory profiling inputs valid once metadata is required.

Scope: the Qwen2.5-VL processor path. Qwen2-VL does not capture `second_per_grid_ts` in the same way, so that would be a separate change. vLLM's video loader already attaches metadata for URL/file inputs; the changed behavior is that bare pre-decoded video arrays without metadata now fail clearly instead of silently using a fallback fps.

Duplicate-work check: I did not find an open PR covering Qwen2.5-VL video metadata forwarding. PR #23058 is Qwen2.5-Omni only, PR #43198 only lets video frame sampling use a request `fps` override, PR #45555 only adds loader-side metadata that this path still dropped, and PR #47407 only bounds M-RoPE positions.

## Test Plan

Run a real `Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct` `LLM.generate` path on an RTX 4090, instrument the live model's `iter_mm_grid_thw`, and compare the temporal `t_factor` for the same video tagged as fps=1.0 and fps=30.0 before, after, and after reverting the fix. Add one CPU regression case to the existing Qwen2-VL processor test file to assert `second_per_grid_ts` tracks fps, run affected Qwen2.5-VL video tests, and run ruff on all changed files.

## Test Result

Upstream main commit `e433634c781dce7ee55563424b8136ad3495c1be` before the fix, same video at two fps values:

| input fps | t_factor |
|---:|---:|
| 1.0 | 0.1669921875 |
| 30.0 | 0.1669921875 |

After the fix:

| input fps | t_factor |
|---:|---:|
| 1.0 | 4.0 |
| 30.0 | 0.1337890625 |

Reverting the patch restored the before behavior:

| input fps | t_factor |
|---:|---:|
| 1.0 | 0.1669921875 |
| 30.0 | 0.1669921875 |

```python
import os
import subprocess

import numpy as np

os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER", "0")
os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING", "0")

import vllm
import vllm.model_executor.models.qwen2_5_vl as q25


def git_head():
    try:
        return subprocess.check_output(
            ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True
        ).strip()
    except Exception:
        return "unknown"


print(f"git_head={git_head()}")
print(f"vllm_import={vllm.__file__}")

captured = []
orig_iter = q25.Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGeneration.iter_mm_grid_thw


def patched_iter(self, mm_features):
    for item in orig_iter(self, mm_features):
        captured.append(float(item[4]))
        yield item


q25.Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGeneration.iter_mm_grid_thw = patched_iter

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

MODEL = os.environ.get("MODEL", "Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct")

num_frames = 64
video = np.zeros((num_frames, 56, 56, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
for frame_idx in range(num_frames):
    video[frame_idx, :, :, 0] = (frame_idx * 5) % 256

prompt = (
    "<|im_start|>user\n"
    "<|vision_start|><|video_pad|><|vision_end|>"
    "Describe the video.<|im_end|>\n"
    "<|im_start|>assistant\n"
)
llm = LLM(
    model=MODEL,
    max_model_len=8192,
    limit_mm_per_prompt={"video": 1, "image": 0},
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.55,
    enforce_eager=True,
    trust_remote_code=True,
)


def metadata(fps):
    return {
        "fps": fps,
        "duration": num_frames / fps,
        "total_num_frames": num_frames,
        "frames_indices": list(range(num_frames)),
        "video_backend": "opencv",
        "do_sample_frames": False,
    }


results = {}
for fps in (1.0, 30.0):
    captured.clear()
    llm.generate(
        {
            "prompt": prompt,
            "multi_modal_data": {"video": [(video, metadata(fps))]},
        },
        SamplingParams(max_tokens=4, temperature=0.0),
    )
    results[fps] = list(captured)
    print(f"input_fps={fps} captured_t_factors={captured}")

fps_ignored = results[1.0] == results[30.0] and bool(results[1.0])
t1 = results.get(1.0, [None])[0]
t30 = results.get(30.0, [None])[0]
print(f"t_factor(fps=1)={t1}  t_factor(fps=30)={t30}")
print(f"FPS_IGNORED_E2E={fps_ignored}")
print("expected_if_honored: fps=1 -> t_factor~4.0 ; fps=30 -> t_factor~0.13")
```

+## Welder: Formally Verifying Kubernetes Cluster Control Planes
 
-For now, the best way to use Anvil is to download the source code and import its components into your controller projects, like what we did for our controller [examples](src/controllers/). Anvil builds and verifies through [`cargo verus`](https://github.com/verus-lang/verus), all third-party dependencies live in the top-level `Cargo.toml`. See [`build.md`](build.md) for how to build, verify, and run controllers.
+Welder is a framework built on top of Anvil for verifying a fleet of Kubernetes controllers. In addition to Anvil's correctness specification, developers formally specify rely-guarantee conditions and liveness dependencies (CORE) of each controller, and verify that controllers respect each other's non-interference requirements and dependencies.
 
-If you want to reproduce the results in the SOSP'26 paper "Welder: Compositional Liveness Verification of Cluster Control Planes", please refer to the [sosp26](https://github.com/anvil-verifier/anvil/tree/sosp26) branch.
+So far, we have built and verified both builtin and custom Kubernetes controllers using Welder: three controllers for managing builtin Kubernetes workloads, including ReplicaSet, Deployment, and StatefulSet, and one custom controller for managing RabbitMQ deployed on Kubernetes. We used the [upstream Kubernetes controllers](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/controller) and the [official RabbitMQ operator](https://github.com/rabbitmq/cluster-operator) as references when building our controllers. We chose these controllers because the Deployment and RabbitMQ controllers depend on the ReplicaSet and StatefulSet controllers respectively, so they require both dependency and non-interference to be satisfied. With Welder, we formally proved that they work together towards their reconciliation goals with respect to those requirements. To avoid interference, we additionally applied some patches that the reference controllers lack, whose absence can cause real conflicts [[kubernetes#138038](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/138038), [kubernetes#41153](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/41153)]. Welder is now merged into Anvil's main branch, and we are using it to build and verify more controllers.

issue.title: script: Make `SharedWorker` tolerant of missing parent event loop

labels.name: S-awaiting-review
labels.description: There is new code that needs to be reviewed.

issue.body:
`SharedWorker`s are meant to outlive their parent event loop. Even
though `SharedWorker`s aren't complete enough to understand having
multiple owners, they shouldn't crash when their parent event loop goes
away. This change prevents that as well as ensuring that the
`WorkerGlobalScope` is always cleaned up even if a panic happens.

Note on testing: I tried very hard to make a test for this, but even
though I could get the worker to crash while the main page was still
alive, for some reason Servo's test harness did not detect the panic in
the worker thread.

Testing: See the note on testing above. This should fix flaky crashes in WPT tests.
Fixes: #47614.

I think the issue is indeed timing related. In the crash handler we print the backtrace first (which takes time, on my system your test happens to crash quite reliably though), and then abort. If the abort happens too late, then its not caught. I'm thinking about adding a flag we set in the crash handler, which could be queried by the wpt-runner when checking for crashes. We could block webdriver responses if a crash is in-progress (to ensure we wait until the backtrace printing is finished and crash), or we could implement the wptrunner check to poll servo if a crash occurred (which could also check the flag).

issue.title: A pure-Rust allocator behind the use-jemalloc feature
issue.body:
### The value of integrating

`components/allocator/lib.rs` selects jemalloc under `#[cfg(all(feature = "use-jemalloc", not(any(windows, target_env = "ohos"))))]`, with `tikv-jemallocator = "0.6.1"` — so Windows and OpenHarmony builds get the platform allocator instead, and the same engine runs on two different allocators depending on the target.

That gap sits directly under Servo's defining characteristic. Parallel layout and style resolution mean the thread that frees a box or a computed-style object is routinely not the thread that created it, so the allocator's cross-thread free path is on the hot path of every page — on whichever allocator that build happened to get. On that path specifically the rusty_alloc README measures **0.83x mimalloc's instructions** (`xthread` — every free performed by a non-owning thread), and against jemalloc its callgrind arms measure **0.84x, 0.89x and 0.98x** whole-program instructions on lua, perl and sqlite under `LD_PRELOAD`.

rusty_alloc is one allocator on every target Servo builds for, in safe Rust with no build script and no `windows`/`ohos` exclusion to maintain. It has 9,261 downloads on crates.io.

Not asking you to change `use-jemalloc` — this would sit behind an off-by-default feature beside it.

### How to integrate

```toml
[features]
rusty-alloc = ["dep:rusty_alloc-api"]   # opt in; `use-jemalloc` unchanged

[dependencies]
rusty_alloc-api = { version = "2.1", optional = true }
```

```rust
#[cfg(feature = "rusty-alloc")]
#[global_allocator]
static ALLOC: rusty_alloc_api::RustyAlloc = rusty_alloc_api::RustyAlloc;
```

Nothing else changes: same layout, same script engine, same embedding API. The interesting comparison is a Windows or OpenHarmony build, since those have no allocator choice at all today.

### Remade With Rust & MATA

We remake C dependencies in safe Rust — allocators, codecs, parsers, compression, identity and storage — so a project can take C out of its build without giving up performance. The rest is at https://github.com/Remade-With-Rust. If this does not suit the project, please close the issue.

issue.title: mach: Support running unit-tests on ohos
issue.body:
- Skip crown unit-tests when cross-compiling
- Skip servoshell unit-tests for ohos, since servoshell pulls in NAPI symbols, which are not available when running as an executable instead of an app.
- Add concept of subcommand to the cargo-build-like command, since all parameters should be added after the subcomand (in this case `run` from `cargo nextest run). Maybe an alternative could be to have command be `[str]` instead, but then we'd need to update all callers and there are places which string compare against `command`.

Note that `CARGO_TARGET_AARCH64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_OHOS_RUNNER` needs to be set to a runner that handles the running of the binaries on the target (ohos-test-runner).

Testing: Currently not covered by automated tests for ohos, but existing supported platforms are executed in CI, so regressions should be caught for those platforms.

issue.title: Support for setup and teardown scripts

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: help wanted
labels.description: Extra attention is needed

issue.body:
Run code/script before any tests / after all the tests

## Usecases
1. Database creation / Database removal
2. Loading variables from external sources (ex. Hasicorp Vault)
3. Setting up / Destroying an external environment

## Configuration suggestion/examples

### With shell code
```
[setup]
shell = "some shell code to be executed before ANY test is started"
timeout = "100s"

[cleanup]
shell = "some shell code to be executed after all tests"
timeout = "10s"
```

### With rust code
```
[setup]
rust = "path/to/setup.rs"
timeout = "10s"

[cleanup]
rust = "path/to/cleanup.rs"
timeout = "15s"
```

comment.body: Has there been any progress on teardown scripts (or would it be easy for a new contributor to add given that setup scripts already exist)? My usecase is I guess a subcase of "Setting up / Destroying an external environment", where I use cargo target runner to push test-cases to a remote device and run the case from there. With pure `cargo test` this works quite well, because all tests from one executable run in one invocation, so one can just delete the executable at the end of the target runner script. With cargo nextest there are many invocations of the same executable, so you'd want to avoid deleting and re-pushing since that costs time. Without teardown scripts theres no way to clean up after the fact, except by checking on each invocation if there are old artifacts on the device which should be cleaned up (which gets complicated by potential concurrent nextest invocations).

issue.title: Wrong Font Name in `is_font` in `mime_classifier`

labels.name: C-untriaged
labels.description: New issues that haven't been triaged yet

issue.body:
**Describe the bug:**
In [mime_classifier.rs](https://github.com/servo/servo/blob/main/components/shared/net/mime_classifier.rs), we have the following code

```Rust
    fn is_font(mt: &Mime) -> bool {
        mt.type_() == mime::FONT ||
            (mt.type_() == mime::APPLICATION &&
                ([
                    "font-cff",
                    "font-off",
                    "font-sfnt",
                    "font-ttf",
                    "font-woff",
                    "vnd.ms-fontobject",
                    "vnd.ms-opentype",
                ]
                .contains(&mt.subtype().as_str())))
    }
```

However, in [WHATWG standard](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#font-mime-type) they correct "application/font-off" into "application/font-otf" in [mimesniff issue 165](https://github.com/whatwg/mimesniff/issues/165)

**To Reproduce:**
Just a typo following previous standard.

**Platform:**
Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS; kernel 7.0.0-28-generic; architecture x86_64

comment.body: Fixed by https://github.com/servo/servo/pull/47904, which was successfully merged as https://github.com/servo/servo/commit/8ae6b28d707c37e050d0de81637b18da4657ad3a, despite github apparently bugging out and not closing the PR.

issue.title: Reduce permissions of try-label job
issue.body:
**Describe the bug:**

#47901 re-adds `checks: write` and `pull-requests: write` to the `run-try` job in try-label.yml. 
This should be removed again, and instead the check writing should happen in the results job (or a dedicated job). 
To that end the artifacts thar are required for etc/ci/report_aggregated_expected_results.py could be uploaded and the artifact-id passed as a job output, that a dedicated job can read. 

The run-try job runs arbitrary code, which could be able to access the GITHUB_TOKEN we inject into the script.
Hence the priviliged step should be pulled out of the job into another one that doesn't run code from forks.

issue.title: ci: update `ci-runners/checkout` action to fix github rate-limit issue
issue.body:
GitHub recently [started rate-limiting][1] the `git fetch` command. This impacted our self-hosted runners where we used bare `git fetch` command which doesn't authenticate with GitHub.

Since `actions/checkout` already handles authenticating using the GITHUB_TOKEN, we have switched our custom `ci-runners/checkout` action in servo/ci-runners#159.  This PR just bumps the workflows to use the new version.

Testing: This has been tested in a [try run]

[1]: https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/206581
[try run]: https://github.com/servo/servo/actions/runs/33872458369/job/101022586287

comment.body: I do wonder if this breaks incremental builds? i think one difference to the old approach might be that the timestamps differ if you do a full checkout like this, vs the old approach. I faintly remember having difficulties with getting incremental builds to work in a docker image, and I think I ended up copying the old approach with the `git switch ...`- I don't think i ever got it fully working, just saying that there might have been a reason beyond what the comment in the ci-runners repo was saying. (not mean to be blocking, avoid rate limits is more important than incremental builds)

issue.title: script: Add ReflectorRoot registry to break cycles

labels.name: S-awaiting-review
labels.description: There is new code that needs to be reviewed.

labels.name: S-needs-rebase
labels.description: There are merge conflict errors.

labels.name: S-awaiting-answer
labels.description: Someone asked a question that requires an answer.

issue.body:
Perma-roots are tricky, since a Perma-rooted Reflector that transitivily references an Object that holds the Reflector means that we have a cycle which Spidermonkey can't collect. 
This leads to leaks, e.g. visible when reloading servo.org. 
To break such cycles, we add a new type `ReflectorRoot`, which allows manually unrooting the Reflector, if it is still alive. We achieve that with an `Rc` and a `Weak` reference, which we register with the Globalscope, so we can manually unroot on pipeline close.

Manual testing: Load servo.org, open a new tab with `about:memory`, measure. Reload the servo.org tab multiple times. Measure memory usage again and compare. After this patch the JS related increase is fixed. 

Testing: We don't have automated tests proving absence of leaks, or that memory is garbage collected.
Fixes: #45262

issue.title: ci / mach: Add some form of deep license scanning
issue.body:
We currently use `carg-deny` and `cargo-about` for license compliance, but they rely on licenses specified in crate `Cargo.toml` being accurate.
However, relying on licenses specified in `Cargo.toml` is not sufficient, as `-sys` crates in practice often do not specify the license that the code they link with requires (machine readable in Cargo.toml `license` field).
To fill this gap we would need some tooling which scans source files and reports actual licenses. I'm not familiar with what tooling is available (free), investigation needed.

review.body: It has come to my attention that gstreamer is LGPL code, which as of now is not in our projects allow-list of licenses. Per my understanding this PR changes the linking of gstreamer from dynamic to static linking, which would change the obligations of servo embedders. IMHO this should be presented to the TSC, clearly explaining what changes, what additional obligations embedders have, and if accepted, clearly document this so embedders enabling the "media" feature are aware of additonal license obligations.

issue.title: Prebuilt llvm-19 depends on libxml2
issue.body:
While trying to update the servo CI image (to ubuntu 26.04), I encountered the following error:

```
160.3       /home/servo_ci/.cache/cargo-ohos/ohos-llvm/19.1.4-79830f/linux-x86_64/llvm/bin/ld.lld: error while loading shared libraries: libxml2.so.2: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
160.3       clang: error: unable to execute command: No such file or directory
```

It seems there is a dependency on `libxml2` (presumably of the llvm toolchain), which the newer llvm-21 toolchain (from the host ubuntu) does not have anymore, so it's not on the system for our llvm-19. 

Not quite clear what to do about it, we could add a setup command (already a PR for that), and check if the linker works and have a recommendation if it fails, but that again is more complexity...


Option worth considering recommended by AI tooling:

>  B — the real fix, upstream in openharmony-rs/ohos-llvm-toolchains. The repack already has RUNPATH=$ORIGIN/../lib, so dropping a libxml2.so.2 into llvm/lib/ makes the toolchain
  self-contained the way the SDK's own LLVM is. Better still, build lld with LLVM_ENABLE_LIBXML2=OFF — it's only used for COFF manifest handling, which is dead weight for OHOS
  targets. This would fix it for every consumer, not just this image.

I was anyway considering compiling clang from source, so perhaps just going to a from-source LLVM-21 build is fine?

issue.title: u32/NonMaxU32 instead of usize in Utf8CodeUnits and friends

labels.name: I-perf-bloat
labels.description: Unnecessary memory usage.

labels.name: A-layout/2020
labels.description: https://github.com/servo/servo/wiki/Layout-2020

issue.body:
In [`servo_base::text`](https://doc.servo.org/servo_base/text/index.html#structs) we define wrapper structs like `Utf8CodeUnits`, `Utf16CodeUnits`, and `Utf32CodeUnits` to represent an offset in a string or its length, to help avoid bugs where one is accidentally used instead of the other. (Rust `&str` uses UTF-8, many DOM APIs use UTF-16 offsets, and much of our font/glyph code uses UTF-32 offsets; even if strings are not necessarily materialized in memory as UTF-16 / UTF-32)

Currently they wrap a `usize` but (on 64-bit platform) they could be made smaller by wrapping `u32` instead. This would reduce memory usage of the box tree and fragment tree. The main question in my opinion is: **how to deal with overflow when converting from `usize`**? It’s possible that trying to have 4+ GiB in a single text node already runs into other limitations, but it’d be nice not to add a new panic. (JS engines have [a practical limit on the length of JS strings](https://stackoverflow.com/a/65570725) but the HTML parser can be fed more at least from the network. At least some parts of DOM code already use `u32` offsets though.)

Going further, we could use [`NonMaxU32`](https://docs.rs/nonmax/latest/nonmax/struct.NonMaxU32.html) to make `Option<Utf*CodeUnits>` smaller, and therefore [`RangeAny`](https://doc.servo.org/servo_base/text/struct.RangeAny.html)`<Utf*CodeUnits>`. [Generic pattern types](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/136574) are not stable in the language yet, so this crate relies on `NonZeroU32` instead. It has a small CPU cost (unconditional/branchless XOR with `u32::MAX`) when wrapping or unwrapping the `u32` value. (Alternatively, if overflow remains a problem, use `NonMaxUsize`. The `Option` optimization is independent from the bit width.)

comment.body:
> how to deal with overflow when converting from usize

Where does the overflow come from? If we cap max string size, shouldn't that be solved?

issue.title: crates 镜像：版本号含 + 的请求被 302 到海外反代，即便该crate已被完整同步至镜像站
issue.body:
### 问题描述 / Bug description

cargo 请求版本号含 + 的包时，会被 302 到海外反代（static-crates-io.proxy.ustclug.org），即便该crate已经完整同步至镜像站上，手动拼接链接可以直接从镜像站获取到，内容也与官方一致。 版本号不含 + 的请求则一切正常。

### **一、正常情况**
用户把 crates.io 源指向 USTC 之后，cargo 就从 USTC 服务器下载包。 cargo 按 包名/版本号/download 拼出下载地址，例如 toml 的 0.9.8 版本：
https://mirrors.ustc.edu.cn/crates.io/api/v1/crates/toml/0.9.8/download
这个地址正常返回该文件。用 curl -sI 请求它，得到 HTTP/1.1 200 OK。

### **二、预期情况**
只要包文件已经同步至 USTC 服务器上，这个地址就应返回 200。

### **三、实际情况**
**3.1 同一个版本，api 路径与静态路径结果不同**
cargo 实际请求的地址：
https://mirrors.ustc.edu.cn/crates.io/api/v1/crates/toml/1.0.2+spec-1.1.0/download
返回 302，Location 指向 
https://static-crates-io.proxy.ustclug.org/crates/toml/toml-1.0.2%2Bspec-1.1.0.crate
该crate在镜像站的静态路径：
https://mirrors.ustc.edu.cn/crates.io/crates/toml/toml-1.0.2+spec-1.1.0.crate
返回 200，56571 字节，SHA256 为 d1dfefef6a142e93f346b64c160934eb13b5594b84ab378133ac6815cb2bd57f， 与 crates.io 官方记录一致。

**3.2 带 + 的版本无一例外返回 302**
测试规模与一个中大型 Rust 项目的依赖树相当：313 个版本，来自 250 个包。 使用 MITM 抓包分析时，测得 cargo 请求包的速率约为 5 次/秒， 因此脚本的请求间隔设置为串行 200 ms，不高于正常构建时的压力。 测试时段选在北京时间 03:10 至 03:20，避开访问高峰。 全程 926 次请求，约 318 MiB 流量，均未跟随重定向。

结果：
含 + 的 100 个版本，api 路径全部返回 302
不含 + 的 213 个版本，api 路径全部返回 200
100 个 302 响应的 Location 全部指向海外反代。
另单独MITM抓包确认了 cargo 自身的行为：为其准备几个含 + 版本号的依赖， 观察到 cargo 收到 302 后确实跟随重定向到海外反代。

**3.3 这 100 个版本的文件都在 USTC 服务器上**
对上述 100 个版本逐一用静态路径请求，全部返回 200，下载内容的 SHA256 全部与 crates.io 官方记录一致。

### **四、影响**
crates.io 上带 + 的版本共 19,125 个，分属 1,545 个包。常用包示例：
toml 1.0.2+spec-1.1.0 —— 891,178,308 次下载
toml_edit 0.25.2+spec-1.1.0 —— 801,410,949 次下载
toml_datetime 1.0.1+spec-1.1.0 —— 768,925,585 次下载
wasi 0.13.1+wasi-0.2.0 —— 746,771,689 次下载
serde_yaml 0.9.34+deprecated —— 396,339,806 次下载
zstd 0.4.16+zstd.1.3.2 —— 380,998,195 次下载
这些包均已同步至镜像站，但请求仍被 302 到海外反代。

### **五、复现**
用 curl -sI 请求下列地址即可重现。
cargo 实际请求的地址，返回 302： 
https://mirrors.ustc.edu.cn/crates.io/api/v1/crates/toml/1.0.2+spec-1.1.0/download
同一版本的静态路径，返回 200： 
https://mirrors.ustc.edu.cn/crates.io/crates/toml/toml-1.0.2+spec-1.1.0.crate
同包不带 + 的版本，返回 200： 
https://mirrors.ustc.edu.cn/crates.io/api/v1/crates/toml/0.9.8/download

comment.body: 感谢反馈，已修复。

issue.title: Reduce allocations when reading small-precision decimals in the Spark connector
issue.body:
## Problem or motivation

`VortexArrowColumnVector.DecimalAccessor` currently reads every non-null Decimal128 value through:

```java
Decimal.apply(accessor.getObject(rowId), precision, scale)
```

Arrow Java's `getObject()` reconstructs a `BigDecimal` through a temporary byte array and `BigInteger`. This conversion is also used for columns with precision 1–18, whose valid unscaled integers fit in a Java `long`. These per-value allocations add overhead when Spark reads decimal columns.

The relevant code is in [VortexArrowColumnVector.java](https://github.com/vortex-data/vortex/blob/a13c246c4985e54362319e789a5a9eea50444ef9/java/vortex-spark/src/main/java/dev/vortex/spark/read/VortexArrowColumnVector.java#L549). I have a local prototype and would like feedback on the approach before opening a PR.

## Proposed solution

Use a specialized accessor for source columns with precision 1–18:

- Read the two native 64-bit words of the Decimal128 value, accounting for native byte order.
- Check that the high word is the sign extension of the low word. If so, construct a `BigDecimal` with `BigDecimal.valueOf(unscaled, sourceScale)` and pass it to the existing `Decimal.apply(value, requestedPrecision, requestedScale)` conversion.
- Use Arrow's existing full-width conversion when the stored integer does not fit in a signed `long`. Wider-precision columns keep the existing accessor.

Spark would continue to handle requested rescaling, rounding, and precision overflow. The prototype retains Spark's expanded Decimal representation to preserve checked integer-cast behavior. Arrow's Decimal128 storage format remains unchanged.

## Additional context

Preliminary JMH measurements compare the prototype with `a13c246c4985e54362319e789a5a9eea50444ef9`. The consumer writes the returned decimals to an `UnsafeRow`. Each Spark version/scenario has three baseline/candidate pairs, with one measured JVM per variant per pair, five 1-second warmup iterations and ten 1-second measurement iterations. Batches contain 4,096 non-null values with alternating signs.

Environment: Amazon Corretto 17.0.16, G1, 512 MiB heap, shared x86_64 KVM host with non-exclusive CPU affinity. Spark versions are 3.5.9/Scala 2.12 and 4.1.2/Scala 2.13.

| Source → requested decimal | Spark 3.5.9, baseline → prototype (ns/value) | Spark 4.1.2, baseline → prototype (ns/value) | Allocation, both versions (B/value) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `(18, 2)` → `(18, 2)` | 68.83 → 35.98 | 66.35 → 35.55 | 192 → 160 |
| `(18, 2)` → `(18, 1)` | 96.64 → 54.93 | 97.50 → 56.57 | 320 → 224 |
| `(38, 2)` → `(38, 2)` | 99.86 → 99.66 | 117.74 → 118.21 | 232 → 232 |

The prototype passes 26 targeted tests on each Spark version, covering precision/scale changes, rounding and overflow, malformed buffers, slices, object independence, negative scales, and checked integer casts. Both native-word layouts are exercised in tests. The same 26 tests per Spark version also pass on a big-endian s390x Temurin 17.0.16 JVM running under QEMU.

Related discussion: [#8197](https://github.com/vortex-data/vortex/pull/8197) considered narrow Arrow Decimal exports and the JNI/Spark Decimal128 assumptions. This proposal optimizes the Java conversion while retaining Decimal128 input.

AI assistance was used to develop the prototype, tests, and this issue draft.

issue.title: fix: propagate LightGBM iteration failures
issue.body:
## Related Issues/PRs

Related to #569 and #728.

This PR addresses the error-handling behavior described in those issues. It does
not attempt to resolve the underlying causes of worker or network failures.

## What changes are proposed in this pull request?

`TrainUtils.updateOneIteration` currently catches exceptions raised during a
LightGBM iteration and sets `state.isFinished = true`.

This makes an iteration failure indistinguishable from legitimate training
completion. In distributed training, if one native worker fails, peer workers
can receive errors such as:

```text
Socket recv error, Connection reset by peer
```

SynapseML then logs the exception as early termination. As a result, the fit can
return a partial model instead of reporting the underlying task failure.

This change:

- logs the iteration failure and rethrows the original exception;
- leaves `state.isFinished` unchanged when an iteration throws;
- preserves the existing behavior when LightGBM legitimately reports completion;
- allows existing Spark task and job failure handling to process the error.

It also adds a deterministic regression test using a failing booster. The test
verifies that the original exception is propagated and the training state is not
marked as finished.

## How is this patch tested?

- [x] I have written tests and confirmed the proposed bug fix works.

The focused `TrainUtilsSuite` passes, including the new regression test:

```text
Iteration failures propagate instead of becoming early termination
```

## Does this PR change any dependencies?

- [x] No. You can skip this section.
- [ ] Yes. Make sure the dependencies are resolved correctly, and list changes here.

## Does this PR add a new feature? If so, have you added samples on website?

issue.title: feat: support S3 compliant filesystems
issue.body:
## Which issue does this PR close?

<!--
We generally require a GitHub issue to be filed for all bug fixes and enhancements and this helps us generate change logs for our releases. You can link an issue to this PR using the GitHub syntax. For example `Closes #123` indicates that this PR will close issue #123.
-->

Closes #5313

## Rationale for this change

Some environments front an S3-compatible service (MinIO, Ceph RGW, Cloudflare R2,
Wasabi, and similar) with a vendor-branded Hadoop filesystem client that registers
its own URL scheme, for example `blob://`, instead of `s3://` or `s3a://`. Today
Comet does not recognize these schemes, so the native Parquet and Iceberg scans
fall back to Spark. This PR lets Comet treat such schemes as aliases for `s3://`
and read them directly, without the caller rewriting URLs.

## What changes are included in this PR?

- New opt-in config `fs.comet.s3Compliant.schemes` (Hadoop key, set via
  `spark.hadoop.*`/SparkConf/core-site.xml at session start). It is a
  comma-separated, case-insensitive list of schemes to treat as S3 aliases. Empty
  by default, so no alias is claimed unless opted in. Short names like `blob` are
  not unique to S3, so the empty default avoids misrouting (for example Azure Blob).
- Native Parquet scan: `normalize_object_store_url` rewrites alias schemes and
  `s3a` to `s3://bucket/key` so the existing `scheme == "s3"` dispatch fires.
- Native Iceberg scan: routes alias schemes to the S3 backend by scheme instead of
  rewriting the URL, preserving the raw `file_path` bytes that iceberg-rust uses for
  exact-match delete-file resolution.
- Vendor-style per-authority Hadoop keys `fs.<scheme>.<authority>.<property>` are
  translated to the `fs.s3a.*` surface (access/secret/session, endpoint, region,
  path-style). Path-style access defaults to enabled when an endpoint is set.
- `CometScanRule` gates alias schemes for both Parquet and Iceberg and emits clear
  fallback messages listing the supported schemes.
- `CometFileKeyUnwrapper` canonicalizes alias schemes so the put and get sides
  agree on one cache key for Parquet encryption key unwrapping.
- Docs: new S3-compliant filesystem scheme section in the datasources user guide.

## How are these changes tested?

- Rust unit tests in `native/core/src/parquet/objectstore/s3_blob_fs_support.rs`
  for URL normalization and alias-scheme detection.
- Scala/Java suites: `NativeConfigSuite`, `CometScanSchemeFallbackSuite`,
  `TestCometFileKeyUnwrapper`, and `CometIcebergNativeScanSuite`.
- End-to-end `blob://` reads against MinIO in `ParquetReadFromS3Suite` and
  `IcebergReadFromS3Suite`, using a `BlobSchemeFileSystem` test shim over
  `S3AFileSystem`

issue.title: fix(terminal): find node-pty in node_modules.asar
issue.body:
Closes #16.

## Problem

The extension fails to activate on VS Code 1.130+. Panel spins forever, no commands registered:

    Error: Asset not found: node-pty/lib/index.js

## Cause

node-pty isn't bundled — the editor's copy is reused so the native binding matches its Electron ABI. But it was only looked for in `<appRoot>/../node_modules`, and 1.130 moved bundled deps into `node_modules.asar`. On 1.132.0 the plain directory keeps just 5 packages; node-pty is in the archive.

The failure is fatal because `shims/node-pty.ts` did its `require` at module scope, so the throw happens while `dist/extension.cjs` is still being evaluated — before `activate` runs. That kills the whole extension, not just terminal sharing.

## Fix

- Probe `node_modules.asar` as well. Electron resolves `require` and `existsSync` inside the archive and redirects native `.node` files to `node_modules.asar.unpacked`, so the editor's own binding is used as before.
- Load node-pty on first spawn instead of at module scope, so a missing binding costs shared terminals rather than the whole extension.

`@vscode/windows-process-tree` shares the resolver and is already lazily imported behind a `win32` guard, so it needs no change.

## Verification

On VS Code 1.132.0 (Electron 42.7.1, ABI 146), loading the built `dist/` with a stubbed `vscode`: before, `extension.cjs` throws while loading; after, it loads, resolves to `.../node_modules.asar/node-pty/lib/index.js`, and spawns a real pty successfully.

`pnpm typecheck`, `build` and `test` (4/4) pass. Remaining lint errors in `README.md` and `src/extension.ts` are pre-existing on `main`.

## Note on #17

#17 fixes the lookup too, but bundles an unrelated `Y.UndoManager` feature and leaves the `require` at module scope, so editors shipping no node-pty still fail activation outright. This PR is activation-only if you'd prefer to ship #16 as a patch release — happy to defer or rebase otherwise.

issue.title: Extension fails to activate: Asset not found: node-pty/lib/index.js (v0.0.23)
issue.body:
# Bug: Extension fails to activate with `Asset not found: node-pty/lib/index.js`

## Environment

| Component | Version |
|-----------|---------|
| OS | Windows 10 / Windows 11 |
| Extension | P2P Live Share v0.1.1 |
| VS Code | 1.130.0 |
| Electron | 42.6.0 |
| Node.js | 24.18.0 |

---

## Error

```text
Error: Asset not found: node-pty/lib/index.js
```

The extension fails immediately during activation.

---

## Steps Already Tried

- Reinstalled the extension
- Installed older versions
- Deleted the extension folder manually
- Tested on **two different Windows PCs**
- Compared extension installation contents
- Same error on both machines

---

## Interesting Observation

The same extension **works correctly** in **Antigravity IDE**.

### Working Environment

| Component | Version |
|-----------|---------|
| IDE | Antigravity IDE 2.0.4 |
| VSCode OSS | 1.107.0 |
| Electron | 39.2.3 |
| Node.js | 22.21.1 |

### Failing Environment

| Component | Version |
|-----------|---------|
| VS Code | 1.130.0 |
| Electron | 42.6.0 |
| Node.js | 24.18.0 |

Additionally:

- The extension worked on a college PC last week.
- It stopped working on the same PC later (possibly after an IDE update).
- The same failure now occurs on my personal PC as well.

---

# Source Code Investigation

I investigated the repository source to understand where the error originates.

The error is thrown by the extension itself.

### `src/terminal/pty/shims/utils.ts`

```ts
export function resolveAsset(path: string) {
  const appRoot = getAppRoot()
  const resolved = resolve(appRoot, '../node_modules', path)

  if (!existsSync(resolved)) {
    window.showErrorMessage(`Asset not found: ${path}`)
    throw new Error(`Asset not found: ${path}`)
  }

  return resolved
}
```

The shim resolves assets from

```text
<appRoot>/../node_modules/
```

instead of resolving them relative to the extension.

---

### `src/terminal/pty/shims/node-pty.ts`

```ts
module.exports = require(resolveAsset('node-pty/lib/index.js'))
```

Activation flow:

```text
Extension activates
        ↓
node-pty shim
        ↓
resolveAsset()
        ↓
resolve(appRoot, "../node_modules", "node-pty/lib/index.js")
        ↓
existsSync() returns false
        ↓
"Asset not found"
        ↓
Extension activation fails
```

---

## Observation

The extension currently assumes that `node-pty` exists inside the VS Code application's `node_modules` directory.

This assumption appears to work in Antigravity (VSCode OSS 1.107), but not in current VS Code 1.130.

As a result,

```ts
existsSync(resolved)
```

returns `false`, causing the extension to fail before activation completes.

---

## Possible Fixes

Some possible approaches:

- Bundle `node-pty` with the extension instead of resolving it from the application installation.
- Resolve `node-pty` relative to the extension installation.
- Gracefully disable terminal sharing if `node-pty` cannot be resolved so that the rest of the collaboration features can still load.

---

## Investigation Note

This investigation was performed with the assistance of AI, but the findings above were verified directly against the repository source before posting this issue.

The analysis traced the activation path to:

- `src/terminal/pty/shims/utils.ts`
- `src/terminal/pty/shims/node-pty.ts`

If my understanding is incorrect or there is another intended code path, I'd be happy to test a fix or provide additional logs.

issue.title: Fix zoom property crash after deleting a stop
issue.body: ## Launch Checklist When a fixed paint value is converted to a zoom function, Maputnik creates exactly two stops. Deleting either one of those two stops leaves a single remaining value. During the transition back to the ordinary field editor, `ZoomProperty` can render with `stops` undefined. It previously called `.map` unconditionally, causing the editor to crash. This PR guards the stop list with optional chaining. The change only protects the render path and does not alter zoom-function conversion or value persistence. Now, the remaining stop's value will be restored after deleting the other stop: The regression test covers `circle-opacity`: 1. Convert a fixed value to a zoom function. 2. Change the second stop's value. 3. Delete the first of the two stops. 4. Verify that the ordinary field editor reappears. 5. Verify that the remaining stop's value is restored. 6. Edit the restored field and verify that the style updates successfully. - [x] Briefly describe the changes in this PR. - [ ] Link to related issues. - [x] Include before/after visuals or gifs if this PR includes visual changes. - [x] Write tests for all new functionality. - [x] Add an entry to `CHANGELOG.md` under the `## main` section.

comment.body:

## Driver

We already have `deleteFunctionStop` in the driver, now the test code uses `await when.deleteFunctionStop(fieldName);` I think this should be OK?

During the test I found another bug, if you convert the background color to a function, and then an expression, the program will crash too. `dataType` is now derived synchronously from the current props during render. This keeps the selected editor consistent with the value it receives and restores the pre-refactor behavior of `getDerivedStateFromProps`.
